code:
(λx.x) z
->β  [x := z] x      # substitute z for every free x in the body
->β  z               # the body was just x, now replaced by z
description: Step through applying the identity function (λx.x) to the argument z using the beta-reduction substitution rule.

steps.description: Line 1 starts with the application `(λx.x) z`, where the function `λx.x` has parameter `x` and body `x`, and `z` is the argument.

steps.answer: Beta reduction rewrites the body `x` with `[x := z] x`, substituting `z` for the free `x` in the body to produce `z`.
steps.question: When we apply the beta-reduction substitution rule to `(λx.x) z`, what substitution notation represents replacing the parameter in the body, and what is the final reduced expression?

steps.description: Line 2 writes out the substitution `[x := z] x`, which replaces every free occurrence of the parameter `x` inside the body `x` with the argument `z`.
Line 3 completes the substitution: because the body was `x` alone, replacing `x` with `z` leaves `z` in normal form.

title: Beta Reduction of the Identity Function
